costGuide.title: Land Rover AJ20P6 Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting an AJ20P6 typically takes 12-16 hours at £65/hr (independent) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes .
paragraphs: The primary cost driver for an AJ20P6 engine replacement is the condition of the cooling system and the mild-hybrid (MHEV) electrical components. Units with documented water pump replacements and no history of MHEV battery or Integrated Starter-Generator (ISG) faults command a slight premium but carry significantly lower long-term risk. Because this is a modern, complex inline-six, a full AJ20P6 rebuild requires specialist diagnostic equipment and precision machining. failures.title: Land Rover AJ20P6 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Water Pump and Cooling System Leaks
items.whatHappens: The plastic water pump housing and associated coolant pipes are prone to cracking and leaking under the high thermal load of the turbocharged inline-six. This leads to coolant loss and potential overheating.
items.repairVsReplace: Replacing the water pump and upgrading to revised coolant pipes is a standard repair. If ignored, overheating can warp the cylinder head, necessitating a full AJ20P6 engine replacement.

items.title: Integrated Starter-Generator (ISG) and MHEV Faults
items.whatHappens: The mild-hybrid system's ISG unit can develop internal electrical faults or bearing wear, triggering warning lights, loss of power, or preventing the engine from starting.
items.repairVsReplace: ISG replacement is a specialised but routine repair for JLR specialists. If the fault is isolated to the ISG, the core engine remains unaffected, though the high cost of the ISG unit sometimes prompts a full engine swap if bundled with other underlying issues.

items.title: Occasional Timing Chain Stretch
items.whatHappens: While significantly more robust than earlier Ingenium designs, some AJ20P6 units can experience minor timing chain stretch or tensioner wear, leading to a faint cold-start rattle.
items.repairVsReplace: Updating the tensioner and chain is a known preventative measure. Catastrophic failure is rare on this generation, but if chain skip occurs, a full unit replacement is required.

failures.goodYearsLine: As a relatively new engine architecture (introduced in 2019), the AJ20P6 has proven significantly more robust than the older V8s it replaced, with failures typically stemming from isolated cooling or MHEV component wear rather than inherent block design flaws .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the AJ20P6
variants.intro: The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, typically visible near the dipstick tube or on the transmission bell housing mating surface, or listed on the VIN plate under the bonnet. The AJ20P6 is frequently confused with the older, naturally aspirated Land Rover 508PN or the supercharged Land Rover 508PS V8s it replaced, as well as the diesel sibling Land Rover AJ20D6. While they share the modern Ingenium inline-six architecture, fitting a diesel AJ20D6 or an older V8 into an AJ20P6 vehicle requires extensive ECU remapping, different engine mounts, and altered cooling and exhaust architecture, making exact code matching critical to avoid costly installation errors.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement AJ20P6 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used AJ20P6 is only advisable for lower-value hosts or project builds, and must come with verifiable proof of strict servicing and no history of MHEV or water pump faults. Without this documented history, the risk of inheriting a failing ISG unit or cracked coolant housing is unacceptably high. Explore our vetted used AJ20P6 engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned AJ20P6 addresses the core weaknesses of this generation. It will include a new water pump, revised coolant piping, and a fully tested or replaced ISG unit. This is the most sensible, cost-effective route for preserving a modern Defender or Range Rover without the unpredictability of a used unit. Compare reconditioned AJ20P6 options

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for high-mileage examples showing early signs of wear, or if the engine has already suffered overheating damage. A quality rebuild should include line-boring, new pistons and rings, and a complete overhaul of the valvetrain and cooling system to exceed factory specifications. Discuss a custom AJ20P6 rebuild

items.question: What is the most common failure on the AJ20P6?
items.answer: The dominant failure patterns on the AJ20P6 are water pump housing cracks, Integrated Starter-Generator (ISG) faults, and occasional timing chain stretch. The plastic water pump housing is prone to leaking under high thermal loads, risking overheating. ISG units can develop internal electrical faults, triggering warning lights or preventing the engine from starting. While more robust than older designs, minor timing chain tensioner wear can still occur at higher mileages.

items.question: Which Land Rover and Jaguar models use the AJ20P6 engine?
items.answer: The 3.0L AJ20P6 (marketed as P400) is fitted to the Land Rover Defender (L663), Range Rover (L460 and late L405), and the Jaguar F-Pace (X761) from 2019 onwards. It serves as the modern, efficient flagship petrol engine, replacing older V8 and V6 architectures. It is mechanically distinct from the diesel AJ20D6 and the older 5.0L V8 variants. Always verify your specific chassis code before ordering a replacement unit.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned AJ20P6 engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned AJ20P6 is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the known vulnerabilities of the cooling system and MHEV components. Used units carry a high risk of inheriting a cracked water pump housing or a failing ISG unit. Proper reconditioning proactively upgrades these specific weak points with revised components and thoroughly tests the mild-hybrid system. Reconditioned units come with a 12 to 24-month warranty, unlike the 3-6 months typical for used engines.

items.question: How do I know if my car has the AJ20P6 and not the 508PS V8 or AJ20D6 diesel?
items.answer: You can confirm your engine code by checking the VIN plate under the bonnet or the stamped code on the engine block near the dipstick tube. The AJ20P6 is an inline-six with a visible MHEV belt-driven starter-generator, lacking the V8 valley or diesel fuel injectors. It is commonly confused with the 508PS V8 or the AJ20D6 diesel, which share similar badging but have entirely different architectures. Fitting the wrong revision will cause severe ECU mapping, mounting, and exhaust compatibility issues.
